Question: If I flash Kali Linux to a USB drive from my Windows laptop (using an ONN drive), can I boot from the USB drive on my MacBook Air?
Answer: Is it a MacBook Air Kali image? My understanding is that Linux still calls ExitBootServices(), which means that it wants another <128K or so of memory back, from the boot process. You can’t call ExitBootServices() on a MacBook Air; it uses the Intel reference UEFI implementation, which has an attribute bug on a number of pages which are required to be maintained after the call, but they are in fact discarded, and a number of other UEFI calls, if made subsequently, will catastrophically fail (the system just reboots, instead of booting Linux). Since many, many people’s UEFI’s have this same bug, being derived from the Intel Reference Implementation, you will find Linux similarly will not UEFI boot on those platforms, either, You can call it a UEFI bug, but since commenting out the call in the Linux source code works around the problem on all platforms, and loses you less than 128K, the only reason for Linux to be stubborn about this is that there are people who want to feel important. If you, on the other hand, comment out the call, and build your own Kali Linux distribution, everything will just work.
